texts.desc:
Masters of close-quarters combat, Warriors unleash devastating attacks powered by their strength.
They build up Rage as they fight, which can be spent to activate powerful class abilities or fuel self-enhancing buffs.
Brutal and relentless, they thrive in the heart of battle.
texts.name: Warrior

talentTrees.desc: Hemorrhage is a bleeding effect whose damage depends on the critical hit that triggered it. As a master of bleeding and critical effects, the warrior specializing in this tree will speed up the fight and increase their rage generation while ensuring that wounded enemies succumb to their injuries.

texts.desc:
Agile and deadly, Rogues specialize in swift, precise strikes and deceiving tactics.
They generate Combo Points through attacks and skills, which are consumed to unleash powerful finishing moves.
Favoring speed and precision over brute force, Rogues excel at dismantling enemies before they can react.
texts.name: Rogue

talentTrees.desc: Lethal Poison is a poison that can be stacked multiple times to amplify its effect. As a master of poisons and debuffs, a rogue specializing in this tree can ensure that their prey slowly succumbs to their wounds.

texts.desc:
Mages are powerful spellcasters who manipulate volatile forces through careful control of their Spark.
Each spell cast consumes Spark, a resource that fuels their magical abilities. But unlike other casters, Mages thrive on momentum : staying above the Flow threshold triggers enhanced effects and bonus power.
texts.name: Mage

talentTrees.desc: Chaincast rewards mages who can chain skills within a set time limit. The reward is a skill with no cooldown that can trigger conduits for free. Mages who specialize in this tree will ensure that enemies are overwhelmed by a barrage of spells and Spark, where conduits reign supreme.

texts.desc:
Priests are devoted spellcasters who channel divine power through sacred Prayers, whispered invocations that call upon celestial forces.
Each Prayer builds over time and can be released to unleash a range of holy effects, from healing and shielding to smiting enemies with radiant force. Mastery lies in choosing the right moment to invoke each blessing.
texts.name: Priest

talentTrees.desc: Sunlight benefits both the priest and their allies by dealing damage with the next final combo attack. A priest specializing in this tree will punish their enemies with the power of light or bless their allies with a barrage of shields and soothing healing.

texts.desc: All it takes to summon the tidal powers is a handful of fishbones and approximately 6 hours.
texts.name: Tidal Totem

texts.desc: All it takes to summon the tidal powers is a handful of fishbones and approximately 6 hours.
texts.name: Tidal Totem

texts.desc: Buzzing around.
texts.name: Angry Bee

texts.desc: Fearing a return of the bloodthirsty humans, Nightling authorities trained these soldiers to scare them away.
texts.name: Nightling Terror

texts.desc: Boars are misunderstood creatures. Farmers hate them, hunters love them, and they feel the exact opposite.
texts.name: Boar

texts.desc: A long-time rival of Al Bearenstein, Niels is reputedly really good at something, but humans have never managed to understand what.
texts.name: Niels Boar

texts.desc: Dwelling inside secluded caverns, Boar sometimes ventures in the outside world to attack a few unsuspecting humans before going back to his quiet life.
texts.name: Boar Burnham

texts.desc: Other venerers repeatedly advised her master that training a hog to hunt wasn't a good idea. 10 years later, no one knows where this man is, but his hog is still wreaking havoc in Skover's woods.
texts.name: Venerer's Hog

texts.desc: This creature looks like an alligator described by an ancient adventurer who never managed to observe one.
texts.name: Crocoboar

texts.desc: This creature looks like an alligator described by an ancient adventurer who never managed to observe one.
texts.name: Crocoboar

texts.desc: One cannot emerge victorious from a fight against a skunk. One can only emerge stinky and shameful, whatever the outcome is.
texts.name: Skunk

texts.desc: There aren’t many preys to catch in the mountains, which means this Leopard is probably hungry.
texts.name: Snow Leopard

texts.desc: According to a theory defended by most Crimson scholars, wolves used to be dogs.
texts.name: Wolf

texts.desc: Wolves get stronger when they eat well, and fiercer when they don't. Somehow, this specimen managed to do both.
texts.name: Alpha Wolf
Coyote
texts.desc: Farmers have always avoided raising poultry on the ground because of the presence of hungry coyotes.
The legend of the dancing wolf can be traced back to the Lost Gods Age. No one has ever actually seen a wolf dance, but we always pick one and suggest it might be doing it while no one is looking.
texts.name: Fangandog
Carmine Hound
texts.desc: The hounds are trained by the Crimson Rams to track down demons. But their voracious appetites often leads them to sniff out truffles instead, much to the delight of the local farmers.

texts.name: Chase
texts.desc: This hound is part of the Ram Patrol, a group of rescue dogs specially trained to respond to any situation, for the glory of the Crimson Rams. The Ram Patrol is on a roll!

Dogma, hound of the blood moon, is the result of Chakram's tireless attempts to crossbreed the canidae of Niflel and Siagarta. Whether the experiment was a success will be left for its victims to decide.
texts.name: Dogma

texts.desc: In their native Merops, the exact working title of these individuals is "Diplomatic Representative in Occupied Territory", which means they were sent to kick your butt.
texts.name: Nepsid Fighter

texts.desc: Only people who live underwater would think of “runner” as an impressive name for infantry units.
texts.name: Nepsid Runner

texts.desc: Skuttle is fast on the ground. Skuttle is fast underwater. Skuttle is fast when she jumps into the air. The only thing that's not fast about Skuttle is her cruel killing method.
texts.name: Skuttle Goldengill

texts.desc: It's no secret that wanted criminals from all around the 9 worlds often end up hiding in Siagarta. Still, Scummy’s reputation as a corrupt individual is so catastrophic he’s even less popular here than among the Meropian court.
texts.name: Scummy BlackGill

texts.desc: This name is a figure of speech. Water can't be broken. But pretty much everything else can be, and you can count on this guy to make sure it is.
texts.name: Nepsid Breakwater

texts.desc: Wavemongers are credited with transforming Atlantis from a banal human settlement into an immortal legend.
texts.name: Nepsid Wavemonger

texts.desc: One of the Oracles’ tasks is to make the sun rise every morning. Sometimes, it takes them a little longer, but they’ve always succeeded so far.
texts.name: Invoked Oracle
Nightling Slayer
texts.desc: Preparing excursions to the highworld of Siagarta, Knight Marish trained these soldiers to protect their platoons from light.

The Nightlord Asmoderator is the living proof that longevity is not always synonymous with good health. This Nightlord has been feeling old for over a century now, which is probably why the Crimson Rams managed to "capture" him.
texts.name: Nightlord Asmoderator

texts.desc: Nightlord Naamahs'tea has always been very polite and a fan of various herbal infusions, which helps him to put into practice the saying ‘Nifel belongs to those who rise early’.
texts.name: Nightlord Naamahs'tea
Nightlord Diabloot
texts.desc: Diabloot is said to always carry a considerable amount of various items with him. When he isn't regenerating in Niflel, he is hunted by numerous adventurers in search of rare items.

texts.name: Nightking Maat Demon
texts.desc: Maat Demon was elevated to the rank of Nightking a century ago by the Nightgod Abaddonk himself. With the return of humans to Siagarta, he now leads the Nightlings’ great crusade, determined to send the humans back to Antelimbo, or six feet under, once and for all.

texts.name: Nightqueen Shaarlize Te'ror
texts.desc: Few Nightladies manage to convince the nightgods to grant them more power; Shaarlize Te'ror almost had to convince them to give her less.
Kobolds who leave the Underworld of Irukal often expect to finally enjoy sunlight and fresh air. Sadly, Siagarta’s mines are also underground.
texts.name: Kobold Miner

texts.desc: The Kobolds make their own cheese, collect their own Spark and craft their own machinery. For everything else, they rely on this kind of unilateral trade humans like to call thievery.
texts.name: Kobold Thief

texts.desc: Kobold workers are autonomous enough not to need a supervisor. However, this is not the case for the many creatures the Kobolds exploit in their farms and mines.
texts.name: Kobold Overseer

texts.desc: Most Kobolds are qualified to beat up humans intruding their mines, but raiders are the only ones who get paid for this specifically.
texts.name: Kobold Raider

texts.desc: Fearing a return of the bloodthirsty humans, Nightling authorities trained these soldiers to scare them away.
texts.name: Nightspawn
Nightbringer Invader
texts.desc: Draculag dreams of becoming the greatest Nightgod in the history of the Nightlings. A short stay in Siagarta at the Crimson Cathedral should cool his ardor.

texts.name: Draculag, aspiring Nightgod
texts.desc: Draculag dreams of becoming the greatest Nightgod in the history of the Nightlings. A short stay in Siagarta at the Crimson Cathedral should cool his ardor.
Hauling a plow through the fields is hard, dull, and bad for your joints. But it's more useful than patrolling with the Crimson army.
texts.name: Crimson Plow Hauler
Gruffy
texts.desc: Gruffy wanted to sail the seas and find treasure. But life as a farmer isn't so bad after all.

texts.name: Crimson Colossus
texts.desc: The recruitment test for ogres in the Crimson Ranks is a simple strength test: carrying a ram on each shoulder and climbing the cathedral steps two at a time. Many fail to count the steps correctly.

texts.name: Crimson Colossus
texts.desc: The recruitment test for ogres in the Crimson Ranks is a simple strength test: carrying a ram on each shoulder and climbing the cathedral steps two at a time. Many fail to count the steps correctly.

texts.name: Ram Stein, the Janitor
texts.desc: The residents of Ramburg can always count on Ram Stein to sing while fixing the elevator if it breaks down.
Is it convenient to be that big when you live in tunnels? No. Does it make the research of ore any easier? No. But does it mean your cheese portion is larger? Also no.
texts.name: Kobold Docker

texts.desc: Heraclette is known across Irukal for having completed all 12 labours: every job involved in the creation of a great fondue, from aurock farming to Spark mining.
texts.name: Heraclette
Kobold Crusher
texts.desc: The crushers use their mace for two things: crushing their enemies and flipping the cheese over the fire pit without burning their paws.
The Nepsids have tried by all means to make gigantism more frequent. However, it only resulted in making their entire population bald.
texts.name: Nepsid Whale
Nepsid Whale of the Lost City

texts.desc: Gilliver is a traveler. In the current state of Nepsid politics, this courtesy title means he's a warrior looking for people to exterminate and riches to plunder.
texts.name: Gilliver

texts.desc: "This is the biggest crab I've ever seen", said the adventurer as an even bigger one approached them from behind.
texts.name: Crab

texts.desc: Krabby is rumored to be a mollusc in disguise. But his very convincing crab shell and even more convincing claw strokes have made this rumor impossible to verify.
texts.name: Krabby Jacob

texts.desc: Before meeting Belzebubbles, humans thought of "ridiculous" and "fearsome" as two mutually exclusive traits.
texts.name: Belzebubbles

texts.desc: Kraba is believed by many to turn fishermen into crabs. This claim cannot be verified but it is intimidating, and negatively impacts crab meat consumption in the region.
texts.name: Kraba the Sorceress

texts.desc: Although he's not a real fiddler crab, the "Crab Maestro" is such a galvanizing musician he inspired his kind to revolt against the Nepsids and embrace piracy.
texts.name: Fiddle Crabstro

texts.desc: Carcinos was once king of the crabs. One would object that crabs don't have a king, but I would answer that it is entirely Carcinos' fault.
texts.name: Carcinos the Proud

texts.desc: This bee might look abnormally big, but nowadays it's the most normal a bee can get.
texts.name: Apix Harvester

texts.desc: It is rare for a Honeybee to live more than a few months, which makes it rather concerning that the oldest Pilgrim records of Beelial date back decades.
texts.name: Beelial
Nightling Patrolfly
texts.desc: Patroflies are, first and foremost, flies, and flies are smashed to bits with a good whack from a slipper : something no self-respecting nightling ever fails to remind his fellow creatures, even if slippers are hard to come by in Niflel.
The Harpies are not a distinct humanoid family. They are just so much stronger, smarter and more organized than their male counterparts that they ended up forming an elite group within the Swarowls.
texts.name: Blackbird Harpy

texts.desc: In Apix vocabulary, "watching" usually also implies "punishing", "slaying" and "making sure humans never come back".
texts.name: Apix Watcher

texts.desc: On her spare time, Mucha is an outstanding painter. But her main occupation is to slay fearsome enemies with her trusted blade, and absorb their souls.
texts.name: Honey Mucha

texts.desc: When the bees discovered that piercing combs and piercing enemy skin were very similar activities, they merged their construction and defense departments.
texts.name: Apix Builder

texts.desc: The morphological disparity between bees is not natural: the higher they rank, the more Spark they're allowed to consume, and the more humanoid they get.
texts.name: Apix Royal Guard

texts.desc: Zucca initially enlisted in the army after noticing how popular the guardians were among worker bees. She now seems to be taking the job seriously, in her own way.
texts.name: Honey Zucca

texts.desc: In a clan known for its extreme work ethic, Bartlebee stands out as a notorious slacker. Thankfully, bodyguards aren't supposed to do much anyway.
texts.name: Bartlebee

texts.desc: Contrary to popular belief, Apix defenders mostly attack.
texts.name: Apix Defender

texts.desc: Messenger of a generation, Bee is always followed by a cohort of followers known as the Junior M.A.F.I.A (Melliferous Apprentices Following the Idol of Apix).
texts.name: Notorious Bee
Nightling Subjugator
texts.desc: Some Nightlings have mastered the art of summoning their kind across space and time. Sometimes the summoning fails, and the subject ends up in two places at once. It’s not a pretty sight.

texts.name: Lady Zaster
texts.desc: Once a respected Nightlord, Zaster was condemned to exile for trying to spare human conspirators during the Guardian War. As a punishment, her soul was entrapped into an island, whose vegetation is a direct manifestation of Zaster's presence.

texts.name: Lady Borgild
texts.desc: Borgild would do anything to find back her lost lover Liv. Especially murdering people. That's something she would have no second thoughts about.
When Spark ledges overflow, they permeate the soil and bring crops to life, which usually attracts weak adventurers looking for easy targets.
texts.name: Rice Seedling

texts.desc: Not many people enjoy the taste of these Onion Seedlings. But they're less dangerous cooked than alive, so we eat them anyway.
texts.name: Onion Seedling

texts.desc: Although garlic is known for its many virtues, I would not recommend approaching this creature to anyone who values their health.
texts.name: Garlic Seedling

texts.desc: A farmer who once tried to prepare a broth with live Turnip Seedlings is credited with inventing the first and deadliest bubble bath in history.
texts.name: Turnip Seedling

texts.desc: Beetroots are known to be bloody, but Maul earned its nickname through repeated, spectacular bursts of rage and violence.
texts.name: Beet the Maul

texts.desc: Barrett has been called a bad seed by Crimson farmhands, but many seedlings are still rooting for it.
texts.name: Seed Barrett

texts.desc: Everything vegetables do is out of norm, because they're not supposed to do anything. Except growing, which is the only thing Vicious has stopped doing.
texts.name: Seed Vicious

texts.desc: In ball games, turnips traditionally played as the ball. That was until Turnip Arker reversed the balance of power.
texts.name: Turnip Arker

texts.desc: Garlic Hooper has become a role model for many seedlings, embodying "the strong, silent type". Most garlic plants are silent, but not all of them can smell that strong.
texts.name: Garlic Hooper

texts.desc: Charles is a polymath who knows its onions in all domains of seedling science: sour grapes, hot potatoes and grassroots organizing.
texts.name: Charles Cabbage

texts.desc: Jared's efforts to cultivate a down-to-earth reputation never bore fruit. Ever since his salad days, people have deemed it full of beans.
texts.name: Jared Lettuce

texts.desc: This used to be a golem. But millenia of elemental pressure have hardened its crystal heart and destroyed pretty much everything else.
texts.name: Sparkle

texts.desc: These creatures have often been confused with urchins, but there are two big differences: these are hundreds of years old, and they will actively try to kill you.
texts.name: Naya Sparkle

texts.desc: When people talk about the eye of a storm, they usually mean something like this.
texts.name: Aoyl Sparkle

texts.desc: When youngsters in Siagarta say "this is fire", what they really mean is "run".
texts.name: Pyrh Sparkle

texts.desc: If you break a golem's husk, a new one will start to aggregate around its little Spark soul. It might take a few thousand years, though.
texts.name: Golem

texts.desc: Ever since this poor creature found a Kobold's earring in the depths of Enripit, it convinced itself that someone would come and steal that treasure.
texts.name: Smeagolem

texts.desc: Originally trained by the Kobolds as a deadly, precise and highly controllable weapon, Goledeneye is neither controllable nor precise, but the Kobolds soon learned it was indeed deadly.
texts.name: Goledeneye

texts.desc: In the mutinied mine of Gorgon's Hollow, the golems have organized a strike, and it won't be a surgical one.
texts.name: Gorgon's Hollow Golem

texts.desc: According to legend, Rascal's head was set ablaze by excess thinking. As another flaming golem once said: "Cogito ergo soot"
texts.name: Blaze Rascal

texts.desc: Known for its fiery words and ardent performances, Arson has become a hot topic in the world of volcanoes.
texts.name: Grill Arson
Aoyl Golem
texts.desc: During severe storms, Aoyl Golems sometimes break apart, only to be carried away by the wind and reassemble several kilometers away.
Although Golatea is made of stone and incapable of speech, its liveliness once captured the heart of famous golem sculptor Magmalion.
texts.name: Golatea

texts.desc: Like most craters, Jimmy is mostly recognized by its emptiness.
texts.name: Jimmy Crater

texts.desc: The slimes have no borders but they have many kings, which has often caused political turmoil in their recent history.
texts.name: Slime King

texts.desc: “Keep your eye in the ball”, a wise Night Slime once said.
texts.name: Night Slime

texts.desc: While Siagarta’s slimes were mostly left to themselves for the last centuries, Niflel’s slimes have spent most of their time around Nightlings, and it shows.
texts.name: Knight Slime

texts.desc: While most vertebrates use their skulls to protect their viscous organs, slimes have taken the opposite path.
texts.name: Green Slime

texts.desc: Blob's name has become a synonym for freedom and change across the Slimes' Kingdom. They still don't have freedom, and not much has really changed, but at least they have Blob Dylan.
texts.name: Blob Dylan

texts.desc: It is not unusual for slimes to provoke laughter, but this one is the first to do it on purpose. Upon discovering that its talent was best appreciated by humans, Lewis started using it as a distraction to devour imprudent travelers.
texts.name: Jelly Lewis

texts.desc: Disguising itself as an Apix larva, this slime managed to get fed by worker bees for several months.
texts.name: Royal Jelly Slime

texts.desc: It is possible to drink the slime with a straw and leave its skull defenseless. That's not to say I recommend it.
texts.name: Honey Slime

texts.desc: Spirits are the Heralds' most devoted servants. But since the War, some have lost their way.
texts.name: Spirit of Tiocha
da'Lida
texts.desc: Once the most celebrated singer among spirits, da'Lida still clings to an unattainable dream for an eternal being: to die on stage.

texts.name: da'Mascus
texts.desc: da'Mascus has always loved the color yellow. That is why he requested a transfer to the Valley of Eternal Autumn.

texts.name: da'Rius
texts.desc: TODO
Not all Crimson Soldiers are violent fanatics, but they all have to act as such and often end up convincing themselves.
texts.name: Crimson Soldier
Crimson Brawler
texts.desc: Some soldiers spend their lives perfecting their swordsmanship; others are simply born with stronger knuckles than usual.

texts.name: Brawler Brahim
texts.desc: Despite his small stature, Brawler Brahim was crowned the grand champion at the Crimson Games.

texts.name: Brawler Mike
texts.desc: Brawler Mike was accused of biting one of his superiors, but no one ever dared to ask him for details about the incident...

texts.name: Brawler Benoit
texts.desc: Brawler Benoit has spent much of his life in the Crimson Ram Special Forces. However, he recently decided to devote himself to boxing.

texts.name: Crimson Executioner
texts.desc: They say that the strongest soldiers wield the army’s large two-handed axes. But when you ask them about it, they say it’s because there’s less blade to clean after duty.

texts.name: Great Executioner Léon
texts.desc: As the Grand Executioner of Ramburg, Léon was given the title of Chief Axecutive Officer by their comrades

texts.name: Captain Druss
texts.desc: Captain Druss wields a two-handed axe like no one else. Some say that if he were to go to war, he could hold a fortress single-handedly.
At first, the Rams thought it was dishonoring to use long-range weapons. It didn't take them long to decide that defeat was even more dishonoring.
texts.name: Crimson Archer
Crimson Cutpurse
texts.desc: The Crimson Rams have a few deserters in their ranks who are running amok in the sewers of Ramburg, armed to the teeth with butcher knives. If you wander in there, it’ll be your money AND your life.

texts.name: Ramface
texts.desc: Ramface just wanted the world. And everything in it.
Visitors in Skover often wonder why the region's farmers are all part of the Crimson army. After meeting the region's turnips, they usually stop asking questions.
texts.name: Crimson Farmhand

texts.desc: When he left the outlaw life to settle down as a celeryman, Pumpkintaro had to change his name. The new one isn't perfect, but it is what it is.
texts.name: Celeryman Pumpkintaro

texts.desc: Agamemnon would have just been a normal captain if it wasn't for his passionate interest in Primeval Age pottery.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Agamemnon

texts.desc: Although he's no longer a page, Ram will forever bear the moniker he earned himself when he accidentally wreaked havoc in a Nepsid camp and miraculously survived.
texts.name: Ram Page

texts.desc: Though she got her nickname from the ramshackle ruins the Rams used to live in, this captain kept it because of the terrible yoke she imposes on her subordinates.
texts.name: Captain Ramshackle

texts.desc: The Crimson Rams used to have two problems: wolf attacks and low meat reserves. Now that Wolfram taught them to eat wolves, they have other, more complicated problems.
texts.name: Captain Wolfram

texts.desc: Miranda would just be a normal captain if it wasn't for her exceptional dancing skills.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Miranda

texts.desc: Sensabille would just be a normal captain if it wasn't for her persistent hearing problems.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Sensabille

texts.desc: Clover would just be a normal captain if it wasn't for her alleged spying activities.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Clover

texts.desc: Carmine would just be a normal captain if it wasn't for his thwarted artistic ambitions.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Carmine

texts.desc: Hector would just be a normal captain if it wasn't for the unfortunate marriage that made him the butt of countless jokes.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Hector

texts.desc: Ben would just be a normal captain if it wasn't for his habit to play with the figurines of the strategy table.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Ben

texts.desc: Roger would be just another captain if it weren’t for his fondness for pineapple pizza.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Roger

texts.desc: Arthur would be just another captain if it hadn’t been for that unfortunate incident involving some goats.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Arthur

texts.desc: Joseph would be just another captain if it weren’t for his undeniable talent for divination.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Joseph

texts.desc: Alex would be just another captain if it weren’t for his passion for weight training.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Alex

texts.desc: Cynthia might be just one captain among many, but her woodlouse breeding business sets her apart.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Cynthia

texts.desc: Katy would be just another captain among many were it not for her penchant for organising pyjama parties.
texts.name: Crimson Captain Katy

texts.desc: It's surprising that the Crimson Rams, who lived on a tiny island for most of their history, specialized in the earth magic of Kyre. But don't bring up the subject around them.
texts.name: Crimson Preacher

texts.desc: Now that the bees have spent five centuries crafting honey with no human interference, beekeeping has become a much tougher job than it once was.
texts.name: Crimson Beekeeper
Crimson Priest
texts.desc: Once a monk learns to drink beer without spilling it on his robe, he is officially eligible to become a priest.
Nepsilon, Envoy of Emperor Nephisto in the land of Skover, doesn’t dislike humans personally. She’s just tasked with ensuring all areas previously inhabited by them are now inhabited by Nepsids.
texts.name: Nepsilon

sequences.comment: Moves to Point A  and uses the Water Breath skill

texts.desc: All it takes to summon the tidal powers is a handful of fishbones and approximately 6 hours.
texts.name: Tidal Totem

texts.desc: Since the Kobolds' sports are very similar to their work, Reblochonk is both the best employee under Ratsar's authority and the regional cheese rolling champion.
texts.name: Reblochonk

texts.desc: A rare successful outsider within the Apix clan, Gatsbee proved their worth by smuggling royal jelly across the continent.
texts.name: Gatsbee

lines.text: $icon(Warning) Take refuge on the shell fragments! $icon(Warning)

texts.desc: Crabgantua, Creature of the Nepsids, was bred and trained to become a humongous warmount. The first part of the plan was such a success that its tamers got devoured before they could get to the second.
texts.name: Crabgantua

texts.desc: "This is the biggest crab I've ever seen", said the adventurer as an even bigger one approached them from behind.
texts.name: Crab of the Lost City

texts.desc: Chuck, Operator of the Kobolds’ transportation system, is tasked with making sure no cheese cargo gets lost and all human trespassers do get lost.
texts.name: Munster Chuck

lines.text: Stalactites have fallen from the ceiling! Hop on them to get to a cannon.

texts.desc: Lady Bee, most humanoid specimen of the Apix clan, aspires to become the most humanoid of all creatures, once the actual humans have been taken care of.
texts.name: Lady Bee
Sponge Blob
texts.desc: Sponge Blob tried to bring some giant fruit shells underwater to use as a new hiding spot. But after getting a craving, he gobbled them all up. Ever since, he’s been hanging out in the cold waters of New Atlaan.
Golcano has been alive for many centuries. Yet, no one ever taught it yet that drooling magma is bad manners.

texts.flavorDesc: Forged in the depths of Irukal, this axe was designed by a people who had never seen a moon in their life, and it shows.
texts.name: Cheese Moon

texts.flavorDesc: Amon, ram-headed god of creation, appeared to Lady Skover in a vision. No one really believed her story at the time, but it did make the Rams appear more legitimate.
texts.name: Amon Ram, the Creator

texts.flavorDesc: If you've been given this sword, someone thinks you can't be trusted with a real one.
texts.name: Light Practice Sword

texts.flavorDesc: To conquer without risk is to triumph without glory. Thankfully, going to battle with that sword makes such a situation very unlikely.
texts.name: Glory

texts.flavorDesc: There is a metaphor at play here: you can see through the blade, but the blade can cut through you. This is the kind of poetry the Apix clan enjoys.
texts.name: Beefury, Blessed Blade of the Farseeker

texts.flavorDesc: This shield is so rudimentary it usually ends up doing more harm than it prevents.
texts.name: Rough Shield

texts.flavorDesc: The best defence is sometimes believed to be attack. Whoever said that has never been hit in the face with a steel shield.
texts.name: Dominion

texts.flavorDesc: According to legend, this is an overcooked slice of pizza from the Primeval Age. Some scholars pretend it is just cheese. Either way, no one ever managed to eat it.
texts.name: Magma Mia

texts.flavorDesc: A creature with three pairs of legs should have more than one kneecap. Crabgantua only had one, but its size and hardness is admirable.
texts.name: Crabgantua's Kneecap

texts.flavorDesc: The sudden evolution of the bees' appearance triggered a sort of identity crisis, after which they started making all their stuff look like wings.
texts.name: Wingsabers

texts.flavorDesc: These weapons have little to do with justice and they certainly aren't pillars, but the Crimson Rams have a taste for metaphors.
texts.name: Twin Pillars of Justice

texts.flavorDesc: Having fins of iron is not necessarily an advantage. In fact, it made the Leviathan slow enough for the fishermen to harvest its precious fins.
texts.name: Iron Fins of the Leviathan

texts.flavorDesc: These training knives were confiscated from their previous bearer for obvious reasons.
texts.name: Rusty Knives

texts.flavorDesc: Like most rodents, Ratsar doesn't have fangs, so he had to steal these. Someday, another toothless creature will probably take them from him too.
texts.name: Twin Fangs of Ratsar

texts.flavorDesc: The former owner of these daggers was none other than the fierce and feared Nightgoddess Nibsham, as cruel as she was addicted to gambling. It is said she lost them playing knucklebones during a siege that dragged on a bit too long during the Great War.
texts.name: Nibsham's Liberators

texts.flavorDesc: At the end of a warrior's arms, these claws look like the gluttonous mouths of two giant snakes.
texts.name: Clawdius

texts.flavorDesc: The purpose of ram horns is to be struck against other horns. For this reason, rams are often represented as twins, so they can strike each other's horns and find purpose in the process.
texts.name: Ramulus & Ramus

texts.flavorDesc: Enripit, once known as the Nightlord who almost stopped the Guardians War, is no longer even able to stop the Kobolds from stealing his sword.
texts.name: Martyr of Enripit

texts.flavorDesc: The institutions of justice are rather uncomplicated in Siagarta. This single axe, for instance, cumulates legislative, judiciary and executive power.
texts.name: Judgement

texts.flavorDesc: The Worldsplitter is known throughout Niflel as the Nightking Maat Demon’s weapon of choice. Many have seen it in action, but few are still alive to tell the tale, and even fewer to say whether this axe is truly capable of splitting a world or not.
texts.name: Worldsplitter

texts.flavorDesc: It's unclear why these specific bees never evolved like their humanoid sisters, but owning one of these tiny hives has become a status symbol for Apix royalty.
texts.name: Pocket Hive

texts.flavorDesc: In the past, Apix princesses ennobled royal guards using their own stingers, but a series of incidents convinced them to use that spear instead.
texts.name: Lady Bee’s Ceremonial Stinger

texts.flavorDesc: Although the legendary Ratsay used his spear to hunt, cook and eat, this tool was mostly remembered as the first toothpick in Kobold history.
texts.name: Gorgon Ratsay’s Toothpick

texts.flavorDesc: Like a sunbeam hitting the dewy blossoms of the morning, this long wooden beam descends vigorously upon the skulls and noses of the unworthy.
texts.name: Radiance
Silhouette of Almaz
texts.flavorDesc: This staff is a powerful relic that was originally used to open the rifts connecting the various worlds to Niflel, the homeworld of the Nightlings.

texts.name: Censer of Wool Hollow
texts.flavorDesc: The High Inquisitor Chakram's favorite staff. He regularly uses the censer to burn herbs at private parties.
A bow is an object of faith and each arrow is a mystery. Will it hit its target? Will its target hit back? Is there still time for a second shot?
texts.name: Credence

texts.flavorDesc: This weapon is a testimony to the Rams' lack of imagination. If something can hurt them, they always picture it wearing a pair of horns.
texts.name: Horns of the Wind

texts.flavorDesc: At one point, this was an Expert's Grimoire, but all the advanced pages are damaged beyond recognition.
texts.name: Apprentice's Grimoire

texts.flavorDesc: Mizan is known for travelling around Merops to learn Naya magic from the Nepsids. No one knows what he did there, but they're no longer taking apprentices.
texts.name: Book of Mi'Mizan

texts.flavorDesc: Before Lord Rulean stole this artifact from the Nepsids, they thought it was responsible for the tides. Luckily, the theft proved that it was in fact useless.
texts.name: Ghost Clams of the Low Tide

texts.flavorDesc: The Nightgoddesses often carry a pair of mirrors with them, which they use to amplify the void and the abyssal emptiness.
texts.name: Mirrors of the Nightgoddesses

texts.flavorDesc: This false scepter is materially identical to a real one. But material reality is of little importance when it comes to rituals.
texts.name: Rehearsal Scepter

texts.flavorDesc: Burning since before the war of the Four Hundred, this candle is widely regarded as the living soul of the legendary Argol Konda.
texts.name: Flame of Argol

texts.flavorDesc: Starflowers are pretty common, but few of them are shooting stars. And even fewer can cut an armor in half.
texts.name: Ipheion, Star Blossom

texts.flavorDesc: A masterpiece of Apix craft, Thornlace is also an expression of the clan's philosophy: beauty is a warning, always laced with danger.
texts.name: Thornlace

texts.flavorDesc: This net can be used to try catching world companions.
texts.name: Large Butterfly Net

texts.flavorDesc: There are two things this shirt cannot protect you from: any kind of damage, and a farmer's tan.
texts.name: White Shirt

texts.flavorDesc: In the rocky grasslands of Azuram, the owls grew so big they started abducting human travelers. Eventually, the travelers got used to it and started using these animals as a means of transport.
texts.name: Azuramean Owl

texts.flavorDesc: On the ethereal grounds that soared above Skover, many animal species had to quickly adapt to a newly aerial environment. In other words, raccoons can fly now.
texts.name: Skoverial Raccoon

texts.flavorDesc: High above Skover’s floating fields, the local creatures had to adjust fast to life in the sky. That’s how the glider-drakes came to be small, friendly dragon pets with soft wings and an easy glide. They flit between the hovering cliffs like playful paper kites, happy to follow anyone who offers a warm hand and a little adventure.
texts.name: Eksodean Dragoon
Skoverian Bat
texts.flavorDesc: The bats of Siagarta have developed the unfortunate habit of drinking their master's blood while they sleep.

texts.name: Pink Moth
texts.flavorDesc: Moths are fascinating creatures capable of releasing powders with various effects: medicinal, hallucinogenic, soporific, poisonous... You should always avoid touching a moth with your fingers.

texts.name: Meropsian Wingfish
texts.flavorDesc: Wingfish are truly strange creatures: nature has endowed them with wings for swimming and fins for flying, which, contrary to what one might think, makes them very poor at both.

texts.name: Enripian Featherbeak
texts.flavorDesc: The two large feathers on the back of the Featherbeaks' wings help them stabilize their flight as they swoop down on their prey. They also play a role in courtship displays: the males with the most colorful feathers are the ones that attract the females.

texts.name: Semeruian Seedbird
texts.flavorDesc: When Seedbirds are hungry, it’s said that they nibble on the tips of their roots and eventually fall to the ground after eating their wings. There, they grow back the following season.

texts.name: Original Paramglider
texts.flavorDesc: During the first attempt to create a special forces unit, the Grand Inquisitor commissioned the development of Paramgliders; unfortunately, the landing was never properly mastered and the project was abandoned.

texts.name: Furious Oculurk
texts.flavorDesc: In the dark lands of Niflel, Oculurks fly ceaselessly, searching for intruders and preys to catch. To prevent their single eye from drying out, they need daily drops from the great infernal river Acherun.

texts.name: Valiant
texts.flavorDesc: In the skies above Ramburg, the pigeon squadron is known for keeping watch over the city, delivering urgent messages, and targeting the plates on the outdoor patios.

texts.flavorDesc: Wolves were trained to sniff out treasures hidden under the debris. Sadly, this one lost the sense of smell after a violent encounter with a skunk.
texts.name: Enripian Wolf
Fountrailian Hound
texts.flavorDesc: In the Crimson city of Ramburg, hounds are prized as a status symbol. A deep red robe indicates that the hound's master is a bloodthirsty monster, even by the Crimsons' standards.

texts.name: Furious Nightdog
texts.flavorDesc: In Niflel, Nightdogs are the preferred means of transport across the shadowy Plains of Hellmist; it is said that, there, the best-trained Nightdogs are capable of finding Nighttruffles.

texts.name: Young Wargcraft
texts.desc: Wargcrafts are a specific species created to allow the bravest heroes to strut their stuff across the world. Over time, as the species has been bred, it has become more docile and is no longer used in combat. Many say that wargcrafts were better in the past.

texts.name: Ebralean Goat
texts.flavorDesc: Humans have tried taking advantage of the goats' spectacular climbing skills. Unfortunately, the poor animals found climbing much harder with humans on their backs.
There are very few Horseans left alive in Siagarta. You’d have a better chance of finding a one-legged spider in the wild than a Sparkling Horsean.
texts.name: Sparkling Horsean

texts.flavorDesc: The most efficient way to travel is not to run fast, but to avoid running into foes. In that regard, the intimidating stare of the hog is more useful than the buttontail's sprint.
texts.name: Meridional Hog

texts.flavorDesc: Skunks were formerly seen as a nuisance. That was before tamers found out the smell problem could be fixed by feeding them only flowers.
texts.name: Primevallean Skunk

texts.flavorDesc: Crocoboars are an endemic species that used to cause many problems. The locals solved this by selling these aggressive creatures as pets across Siagarta.
texts.name: Eksodean Crocoboar
Rinuhrian Warram
texts.flavorDesc: Warrams are sturdy creatures, capable of bringing down watchtowers with a single headbutt. Fights between males in the Ebral highlands can be heard as far away as Ramburg. Their strength has inspired the Crimson Rams, who have chosen them as their emblem.

texts.name: Aegis
texts.desc: Aegis is Chakram’s faithful steed. When Chakram turned his back on humans and pledged his allegiance to the demons, his companion could not bring himself to abandon him and now bears the scars of that betrayal.

texts.flavorDesc: Originally bred by farmers to rid their crops of midges, leggybugs eventually grew big enough to be employed as draught animals, and later as recreational vehicles.
texts.name: Nescentine Leggybug
Meropsian Crab
texts.flavorDesc: Legend has it that the first crab used as a mount was won by a fisherman during a charades match against a Nepsid. The word to guess was "crab". The match lasted two days.
